رَائِقٌ Anything eaten, or drunk, عَلَى الرِّيقِ [i. e. in the state of fasting; before breakfast]. (K.) See also رَيْقٌ, in two places. ―
-b2- And see رِيقٌ, likewise in two places. ―
-b3- Also (assumed tropical:) Empty-handed. (K.) You say, جَآءَ رَائِقًا (assumed tropical:) He came empty [-handed]. (JK.) ＝
-A2- Also Pure; (As, K;) applied to musk, and to anything. (As, TA.) [Mentioned also in art. روق.] ＝
-A3- Also said to signify ثوب عجن بالمسك [i. e. عُجِنَ بِالمِسْكِ, app. meaning that it is an epithet applied to a garment as signifying Sprinkled with musk and then pressed, or kneaded]. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
